model: Option B — concept ontology (main/data/ontology/sulfur_terms.json) + separate lexeme registry
purpose: A lexeme is a language-specific naming form that refers to a language-neutral concept. lexeme -> names -> concept.
rules: The lexeme registry owns LEXICAL IDENTITY only.

It does NOT own evidence/source linkage. Forward links (evidence -> lexeme, evidence -> source, evidence -> claim) are owned by the evidence store. The reverse view (lexeme -> supporting evidence) is DERIVED by an index/validator/query, never stored here. One relationship fact -> one authoritative direction -> reverse edges derived.
Every lexeme MUST resolve to exactly one CONCEPT-ELIGIBLE ontology node (see main/data/ontology_node_roles.json). Existence of an ontology term_id does NOT make it a valid concept target.
concept_id is an identifier, NOT a language claim. Concepts are language-neutral.

Lexeme language is ORTHOGONAL to geography: a LEX-DE-* lexeme is German-LANGUAGE, not Germany-GEOGRAPHY. Geography is never derived from lexeme language; it is a separate evidence-qualified relationship.

registration_state is the lexeme's lexical-identity state (manually governed). Whether a lexeme is evidence-supported is a DERIVED fact computed from the evidence store, never a second manually-editable authority.
A lexeme NEVER creates a route or URL. Knowledge Object Before URL is absolute.
Free-text strings must not substitute for lexeme IDs in governed evidence.
concept_binding: concept_id resolves to a concept-eligible term_id in main/data/ontology/sulfur_terms.json (per ontology_node_roles.json).
derived_view_note: lexeme -> supporting evidence is computed by scanning main/data/evidence/*.json for records whose lexeme_ids contain this lexeme_id. It is not stored on the lexeme.

id_rules.rule: Production lexeme IDs start 'LEX-'. Test fixtures start 'TEST-LEX-'. A governed lexeme MUST NOT use a TEST- identifier.

lexemes.notes: Form observed in a German Lexikon der Chemie (Spektrum.de) dictionary entry for the MoS2 concept. 'observed_usage' — the narrowest supported relationship: the approved claim (CLM-TERM-MOS2-DE-001) establishes only that a dictionary entry exists supporting cautious terminology framing, NOT a general 'accepted' German-form status. Lexeme-level, German-language (not Germany-geography). Public URL NOT authorized. Evidence support is derived from the evidence store, not stored here.
Dictionary sense: Merriam-Webster defines 'bisulfide' as 'disulfide' (first known use 1831). 'bisulfide' is polysemous; see LEX-EN-BISULFIDE-002. (Recovery-03)
Database-synonym sense: PubChem lists 'bisulfide' among the synonyms of HS- (CID 5047209). Supported only by boundary (database) evidence, not by an admitted lexical authority. (Recovery-03)
Merriam-Webster: 'an acid sulfite'. Not a sulfide. (Recovery-03)
IUPAC 2005 IR-8.5 accepted abbreviated hydrogen name for HSO3-. (Recovery-03)
IUPAC 2005 name for the S2 2- anion. (Recovery-03)
IUPAC 2005 name for S2 2- derived from the parent hydride. (Recovery-03)
Spektrum Lexikon der Chemie uses 'Hydrogensulfide' for the salts MIHS; DWDS does not list it in its contemporary lexical sources. (Recovery-03)

Observed in German industry usage for HS- (Badger Meter; contextual, not admitted). DWDS does not list it in its contemporary lexical sources; Duden has no entry. Not a lexicographically established German term. (Recovery-03)
